sanskrit: saṃkaro narakāyaiva kulaghnānāṃ kulasya ca patanti pitaro hy eṣāṃ luptapiṇḍodakakriyāḥ
english: Such confusion leads only to hell, both for the destroyers of the family and for the family itself; for their ancestors fall, deprived of the offerings of rice and water.

sanskrit: doṣair etaiḥ kulaghnānāṃ varṇasaṃkarakārakaiḥ utsādyante jātidharmāḥ kuladharmāś ca śāśvatāḥ
english: By these misdeeds of the destroyers of the family, which bring about the confusion of castes, the eternal laws of caste and the eternal laws of the family are uprooted.

sanskrit: utsannakuladharmāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ janārdana narake niyataṃ vāso bhavatīty anuśuśruma
english: And for those men whose family laws have been destroyed, O Janārdana, a dwelling in hell is ordained — so we have heard handed down.

sanskrit: aho bata mahat pāpaṃ kartuṃ vyavasitā vayam yad rājyasukhalobhena hantuṃ svajanam udyatāḥ
english: Alas! We are resolved to commit a great sin, in that, out of greed for the pleasures of kingship, we stand ready to slay our own kin.

sanskrit: yadi mām apratīkāram aśastraṃ śastrapāṇayaḥ dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyus tan me kṣemataraṃ bhavet
english: If the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, weapons in hand, were to slay me in battle, unresisting and unarmed, that would be the more blessed end for me.

sanskrit: evam uktvārjunaḥ saṃkhye rathopastha upāviśat visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ
english: Having spoken thus on the field of battle, Arjuna sank down upon the seat of the chariot, casting aside his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca taṃ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭam aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam viṣīdantam idaṃ vākyam uvāca madhusūdanaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: To him thus overcome by pity, his troubled eyes brimming with tears, despondent, the Slayer of Madhu spoke these words.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca kutas tvā kaśmalam idaṃ viṣame samupasthitam anāryajuṣṭam asvargyam akīrtikaram arjuna
english: The Blessed Lord said: Whence has this faintheartedness come upon you in this hour of peril, O Arjuna — a thing unworthy of the noble, barring the way to heaven, bringing dishonor?

sanskrit: klaibyaṃ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitat tvayy upapadyate kṣudraṃ hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha paraṃtapa
english: Yield not to unmanliness, O Pārtha; it does not become you. Cast off this base weakness of heart and arise, scorcher of foes!

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kathaṃ bhīṣmam ahaṃ saṃkhye droṇaṃ ca madhusūdana iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjārhāv arisūdana
english: Arjuna said: How, O Slayer of Madhu, shall I fight back with arrows in battle against Bhīṣma and Droṇa, who are worthy of my worship, O Slayer of foes?

sanskrit: gurūn ahatvā hi mahānubhāvāñ; śreyo bhoktuṃ bhaikṣam apīha loke hatvārthakāmāṃs tu gurūn ihaiva; bhuñjīya bhogān rudhirapradigdhān
english: For it were better in this world to eat even the bread of beggary than to slay these noble-souled elders. If I slew my elders, though they covet gain, I should taste, here and now, only delights smeared with blood.

sanskrit: na caitad vidmaḥ kataran no garīyo; yad vā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ yān eva hatvā na jijīviṣāmas; te 'vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ
english: Nor do we know which is the better for us — that we should conquer them, or that they should conquer us. Those whom if we slew we should not wish to live — the very sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — stand arrayed against us.

sanskrit: kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ; pṛcchāmi tvāṃ dharmasaṃmūḍhacetāḥ yac chreyaḥ syān niścitaṃ brūhi tan me; śiṣyas te 'haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam
english: My very nature undone by the taint of pitiable weakness, my mind bewildered as to what is right, I ask you: tell me with certainty what is the better course. I am your disciple; instruct me, who have taken refuge in you.

sanskrit: na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyād; yac chokam ucchoṣaṇam indriyāṇām avāpya bhūmāv asapatnam ṛddhaṃ; rājyaṃ surāṇām api cādhipatyam
english: For I do not see what could dispel this grief that withers my senses, even were I to win on earth an unrivaled and prosperous kingdom, or even lordship over the gods.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ guḍākeśaḥ paraṃtapa na yotsya iti govindam uktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha
english: Saṃjaya said: Having spoken thus to Hṛṣīkeśa, Guḍākeśa, the scorcher of foes, said to Govinda, "I shall not fight," and fell silent.

sanskrit: tam uvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasann iva bhārata senayor ubhayor madhye viṣīdantam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: To him, O descendant of Bharata, as he sat despondent between the two armies, Hṛṣīkeśa spoke these words, as if with a smile.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca aśocyān anvaśocas tvaṃ prajñāvādāṃś ca bhāṣase gatāsūn agatāsūṃś ca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ
english: The Blessed Lord said: You have grieved for those who should not be grieved for, yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.

sanskrit: na tv evāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayam ataḥ param
english: Never was there a time when I was not, nor you, nor these lords of men; nor shall any of us ever cease to be hereafter.

sanskrit: dehino 'smin yathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā tathā dehāntaraprāptir dhīras tatra na muhyati
english: As the embodied soul passes, within this body, through childhood, youth, and old age, so does it pass to another body. The steadfast are not bewildered by this.

sanskrit: mātrāsparśās tu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ āgamāpāyino 'nityās tāṃs titikṣasva bhārata
english: The contacts of the senses with their objects, O son of Kuntī, give rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and are impermanent; endure them, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: yaṃ hi na vyathayanty ete puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha samaduḥkhasukhaṃ dhīraṃ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate
english: The man whom these do not disturb, O bull among men — the steadfast one, alike in pain and pleasure — he is fit for immortality.

sanskrit: nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ ubhayor api dṛṣṭo 'ntas tv anayos tattvadarśibhiḥ
english: Of the unreal there is no being; of the real there is no ceasing to be. The truth of both has been perceived by the seers of reality.

sanskrit: avināśi tu tad viddhi yena sarvam idaṃ tatam vināśam avyayasyāsya na kaś cit kartum arhati
english: Know that to be indestructible by which all this is pervaded. None can bring about the destruction of this imperishable one.

sanskrit: antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ anāśino 'prameyasya tasmād yudhyasva bhārata
english: These bodies of the eternal embodied soul are said to come to an end, while it is indestructible and immeasurable. Therefore fight, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaś cainaṃ manyate hatam ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate
english: He who thinks this one to be a slayer, and he who thinks it slain — neither of them understands. It neither slays nor is slain.

sanskrit: na jāyate mriyate vā kadā cin; nāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo; na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
english: It is never born, nor does it ever die; having come to be, it shall not again cease to be. Unborn, eternal, everlasting, ancient, it is not slain when the body is slain.

sanskrit: vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enam ajam avyayam kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam
english: He who knows this one to be indestructible, eternal, unborn, and undiminishing — how, O Pārtha, can such a man cause anyone to be slain, or slay anyone?

sanskrit: vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya; navāni gṛhṇāti naro 'parāṇi tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāny; anyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī
english: As a man casts off worn-out garments and takes on others that are new, so the embodied soul casts off worn-out bodies and enters into others that are new.

sanskrit: nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ na cainaṃ kledayanty āpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ
english: Weapons do not cut it, fire does not burn it, waters do not wet it, nor does the wind wither it.

sanskrit: acchedyo 'yam adāhyo 'yam akledyo 'śoṣya eva ca nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇur acalo 'yaṃ sanātanaḥ
english: It cannot be cut, it cannot be burned, it cannot be wetted, nor can it be dried. Eternal, all-pervading, fixed, unmoving, it is everlasting.

sanskrit: avyakto 'yam acintyo 'yam avikāryo 'yam ucyate tasmād evaṃ viditvainaṃ nānuśocitum arhasi
english: It is said to be unmanifest, unthinkable, and unchanging. Therefore, knowing it to be such, you ought not to grieve.

sanskrit: atha cainaṃ nityajātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam tathāpi tvaṃ mahābāho nainaṃ śocitum arhasi
english: And even if you should think it to be ever born and ever dying, even then, O mighty-armed one, you ought not to grieve for it.

sanskrit: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca tasmād aparihārye 'rthe na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi
english: For of one that is born, death is certain; and of one that is dead, birth is certain. Therefore, over a thing that cannot be averted, you ought not to grieve.

sanskrit: avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyaktamadhyāni bhārata avyaktanidhanāny eva tatra kā paridevanā
english: Beings are unmanifest in their beginnings, manifest in their middle states, and unmanifest again at their end, O descendant of Bharata. What occasion, then, for lament?

sanskrit: āścaryavat paśyati kaś cid enam; āścaryavad vadati tathaiva cānyaḥ āścaryavac cainam anyaḥ śṛṇoti; śrutvāpy enaṃ veda na caiva kaś cit
english: One beholds it as a marvel; another likewise speaks of it as a marvel; and another hears of it as a marvel; yet even having heard, no one truly knows it.

sanskrit: dehī nityam avadhyo 'yaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi
english: This embodied soul, dwelling in the body of every being, is eternally inviolable, O descendant of Bharata. Therefore you ought not to grieve for any creature.

sanskrit: svadharmam api cāvekṣya na vikampitum arhasi dharmyād dhi yuddhāc chreyo 'nyat kṣatriyasya na vidyate
english: And looking to your own dharma, you ought not to waver; for there is no greater good for a warrior than a righteous battle.

sanskrit: yadṛcchayā copapannaṃ svargadvāram apāvṛtam sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddham īdṛśam
english: Happy are the warriors, O Pārtha, to whom comes unsought such a battle, an open gate to heaven.

sanskrit: atha cet tvam imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi tataḥ svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpam avāpsyasi
english: But if you will not wage this righteous war, then, forsaking your own dharma and your honor, you shall incur sin.

sanskrit: akīrtiṃ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te 'vyayām saṃbhāvitasya cākīrtir maraṇād atiricyate
english: People, too, will tell of your undying disgrace; and for one held in honor, dishonor is worse than death.

sanskrit: bhayād raṇād uparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
english: The great warriors will think that you withdrew from the battle out of fear; and you who were once highly esteemed by them will fall into contempt.

sanskrit: avācyavādāṃś ca bahūn vadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ nindantas tava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim
english: And your enemies will speak many unspeakable words, scorning your prowess. What could be more painful than that?

sanskrit: hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm tasmād uttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ
english: Either slain, you shall attain heaven, or victorious, you shall enjoy the earth. Therefore arise, O son of Kuntī, resolved upon battle.

sanskrit: sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpam avāpsyasi
english: Holding pleasure and pain alike, gain and loss, victory and defeat, gird yourself then for battle; thus you shall incur no sin.

sanskrit: eṣā te 'bhihitā sāṃkhye buddhir yoge tv imāṃ śṛṇu buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi
english: This wisdom has been declared to you according to Sāṃkhya; now hear it as it pertains to yoga, by which understanding, O Pārtha, once joined with it, you shall cast off the bondage of action.

sanskrit: nehābhikramanāśo 'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate svalpam apy asya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt
english: In this path no effort is ever lost, and no obstacle arises; even a little of this dharma saves one from great fear.

sanskrit: vyavasāyātmikā buddhir ekeha kurunandana bahuśākhā hy anantāś ca buddhayo 'vyavasāyinām
english: Here the resolute understanding is one and single, O joy of the Kurus; but the thoughts of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.

sanskrit: yām imāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadanty avipaścitaḥ vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyad astīti vādinaḥ
english: The flowery speech that the unwise utter, O Pārtha — those who delight in the letter of the Veda, declaring that there is nothing more —

sanskrit: kāmātmānaḥ svargaparā janmakarmaphalapradām kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati
english: full of desire, intent on heaven, promising rebirth as the fruit of works, thronged with manifold rites directed toward enjoyment and power —

sanskrit: bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasām vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate
english: in those attached to enjoyment and power, whose minds are carried away by that speech, the resolute understanding fixed in contemplation is not established.

sanskrit: traiguṇyaviṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna nirdvaṃdvo nityasattvastho niryogakṣema ātmavān
english: The Vedas have the three guṇas for their province; be free of the three guṇas, O Arjuna. Be free of the pairs of opposites, ever poised in purity, indifferent to acquisition and possession, master of yourself.

sanskrit: yāvān artha udapāne sarvataḥ saṃplutodake tāvān sarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ
english: As much use as there is in a well when water floods on every side, so much is there in all the Vedas for the brāhmaṇa who truly knows.

sanskrit: karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadā cana mā karmaphalahetur bhūr mā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi
english: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Let not the fruit of action be your motive, nor let your attachment be to inaction.

sanskrit: yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanaṃjaya siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate
english: Established in yoga, perform your actions, abandoning attachment, O Dhanaṃjaya, alike in success and in failure; for this evenness of mind is called yoga.

sanskrit: dūreṇa hy avaraṃ karma buddhiyogād dhanaṃjaya buddhau śaraṇam anviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ
english: For action is far inferior to the yoga of understanding, O Dhanaṃjaya. Seek refuge in understanding; pitiable are those who act for the sake of fruits.

sanskrit: buddhiyukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam
english: He who is joined to understanding casts off, here in this life, both good deeds and evil deeds. Therefore devote yourself to yoga; yoga is skill in action.

sanskrit: karmajaṃ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ padaṃ gacchanty anāmayam
english: For the wise, joined to understanding, abandoning the fruit born of action, are freed from the bondage of birth and reach the state beyond all ill.

sanskrit: yadā te mohakalilaṃ buddhir vyatitariṣyati tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca
english: When your understanding crosses beyond the thicket of delusion, then you shall grow indifferent to all that has been heard and all that is yet to be heard.

sanskrit: śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā samādhāv acalā buddhis tadā yogam avāpsyasi
english: When your understanding, bewildered by scripture, shall stand unmoving and unwavering, fixed in contemplation, then you shall attain to yoga.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kim āsīta vrajeta kim
english: Arjuna said: What is the description of the man of steadfast wisdom, who abides in contemplation, O Keśava? How does the man of steady mind speak, how does he sit, how does he walk?

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha manogatān ātmany evātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñas tadocyate
english: The Blessed Lord said: When a man casts off all the desires that come into his mind, O Pārtha, content in the Self by the Self alone, then is he called a man of steadfast wisdom.

sanskrit: duḥkheṣv anudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhīr munir ucyate
english: He whose mind is untroubled amid sorrows, who has no craving for pleasures, and from whom longing, fear, and anger have departed — he is called a sage of steady mind.

sanskrit: yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehas tat tat prāpya śubhāśubham nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
english: He who is without attachment on every side, who, meeting with whatever is good or evil, neither rejoices nor recoils — his wisdom stands firm.

sanskrit: yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo 'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
english: And when, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs from every side, he withdraws his senses from the objects of sense, his wisdom stands firm.

sanskrit: viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ rasavarjaṃ raso 'py asya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate
english: The objects of sense turn away from the embodied one who abstains from them, yet the relish for them remains; but even that relish departs once he has beheld the Supreme.

sanskrit: yatato hy api kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ
english: For even in the man of discernment who strives, O son of Kuntī, the turbulent senses carry away the mind by force.

sanskrit: tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta matparaḥ vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
english: Having restrained all these, let him sit, steadfast in yoga, intent on Me; for he whose senses are mastered — his wisdom stands firm.

sanskrit: dhyāyato viṣayān puṃsaḥ saṅgas teṣūpajāyate saṅgāt saṃjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate
english: In the man who dwells in thought upon the objects of sense, attachment to them is born; from attachment springs desire, and from desire arises anger.

sanskrit: krodhād bhavati saṃmohaḥ saṃmohāt smṛtivibhramaḥ smṛtibhraṃśād buddhināśo buddhināśāt praṇaśyati
english: From anger comes delusion, from delusion the wandering of memory; from the loss of memory comes the ruin of understanding, and from the ruin of understanding he perishes.

sanskrit: rāgadveṣaviyuktais tu viṣayān indriyaiś caran ātmavaśyair vidheyātmā prasādam adhigacchati
english: But the man of disciplined self, moving among the objects of sense with senses freed from longing and aversion and brought under his own control, attains to serenity.

sanskrit: prasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānir asyopajāyate prasannacetaso hy āśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate
english: In that serenity there arises for him the cessation of all his sorrows; for in the man of serene mind the understanding soon becomes firmly established.

sanskrit: nāsti buddhir ayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā na cābhāvayataḥ śāntir aśāntasya kutaḥ sukham
english: There is no understanding for the undisciplined, nor for the undisciplined any power of contemplation; and for him without contemplation there is no peace — and for the peaceless, whence happiness?

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yan mano 'nuvidhīyate tad asya harati prajñāṃ vāyur nāvam ivāmbhasi
english: For when the mind yields to the roving senses, it carries away his wisdom, as the wind carries away a ship upon the waters.

sanskrit: tasmād yasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
english: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, he whose senses are wholly restrained from the objects of sense — his wisdom stands firm.

sanskrit: yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ
english: In that which is night for all beings, the man of self-restraint is awake; and that in which all beings are awake is night for the sage who sees.

sanskrit: āpūryamāṇam acalapratiṣṭhaṃ; samudram āpaḥ praviśanti yadvat tadvat kāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve; sa śāntim āpnoti na kāmakāmī
english: As the waters enter the ocean, which, ever filling, abides unmoved, so he into whom all desires enter attains peace — not he who lusts after desires.

sanskrit: vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumāṃś carati niḥspṛhaḥ nirmamo nirahaṃkāraḥ sa śāntim adhigacchati
english: The man who, abandoning all desires, moves about free from longing, without the sense of "mine" and without egoism — he attains to peace.

sanskrit: eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati sthitvāsyām antakāle 'pi brahmanirvāṇam ṛcchati
english: This is the state of Brahman, O Pārtha; attaining it, none is deluded. Abiding in it even at the hour of death, one reaches the nirvāṇa of Brahman.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca jyāyasī cet karmaṇas te matā buddhir janārdana tat kiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava
english: Arjuna said: If you hold understanding to be better than action, O Janārdana, then why do you urge me to this terrible deed, O Keśava?

sanskrit: vyāmiśreṇaiva vākyena buddhiṃ mohayasīva me tad ekaṃ vada niścitya yena śreyo 'ham āpnuyām
english: With words that seem confused, you bewilder, as it were, my understanding. Tell me, therefore, with certainty, the one path by which I may attain the higher good.
